raw_graphql_pull_request.body: > **Depends on #61667.** Draft until the consumer slot quarantine lands; see "Merge order" below. ## Purpose Part of #63602 (gap 2). When a P2P load times out (`_P2P_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S` 10 s for a symmetric-P2P fetch, `_PD_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S` 30 s for a PD fetch), the consumer sends `AbortFetchMsg`. If no `AbortAck` arrives within `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` (5 s), `ClientRole.collect_results()` fails that one load, but the session stays up. Every later fetch routed to the same stuck peer then waits out both timeouts again: 15 s per P2P request, 35 s per PD request. The GPU run in #63602 (before the per-mode split in #63781) showed exactly this: loads to the replacement peer took 40.1–40.2 s and 0/400 pulls succeeded. A missed `AbortAck` means the peer has stopped confirming that its WRITEs ended, and this side can't tell whether they stopped. This PR treats it as a data-plane fault: - `ClientRole` records the first load whose `AbortAck` timed out (`expired_abort_ack`). The load still fails exactly as before. - `P2PSession.poll()` checks it right after `_escalate_peer_fault()` and calls `_disconnect("abort ack timed out")`. It sends a best-effort `DisconnectMsg` and marks the connection dead, the same path the lookup-response timeout already uses. Like `_escalate_peer_fault()`, it does nothing if the session already died earlier in the same poll (for example, the peer's `DisconnectMsg`), so a clean disconnect is not reported as a data-plane fault. - `data_plane_fault` also reports this cause, so the manager's reap applies the existing data-plane reconnect backoff (1 s doubling up to 60 s) instead of immediately reconnecting to the stuck peer. The reap already fails the peer's other in-flight loads and unresolved probes, so they prefill locally. There are no manager changes. This is the consumer-side bound. It works even when the source's control path is broken, which is exactly when the source-side stall deadline proposed in #63602 can't help. ## Trade-off: a slow but healthy peer is also disconnected The source holds the `AbortAck` until NIXL reports every aborted WRITE terminal (`_pending_aborts` / `_slow_aborts` in the server role); it never force-releases one, and only logs past `_CANCEL_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S` (10 s). So a large WRITE that is still progressing more than 5 s after the abort now ends the whole session: the peer's other loads fail and prefill locally, and the reconnect backoff starts. This is deliberate. On `main` that load already fails at the same moment; this PR adds the collateral failures and the backoff. The consumer can't tell a slow WRITE from a stuck one, and a peer that can't finish a single transfer within the load timeout plus 5 s is not worth routing more fetches to. Keeping the session is exactly what made every later request wait out both timeouts again. I have not measured the largest single transfer under load against the 5 s bound. On links where one WRITE can legitimately exceed it, `_ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S` (shared with the existing per-load failure) is the knob; this PR doesn't change it. ## Merge order Without #61667, a failed load hands its destination slots back through `complete_write(..., False)` while the source's WRITE may still land in them. On `main` that already happens for the one load whose `AbortAck` timed out. This PR's disconnect fails *every* in-flight load to that peer, so it widens the same window, and the source's abort drain has no deadline (gap 2 in #63602). With #61667, those slots stay quarantined until `TransferDone`/`AbortAck`, or a fencing guarantee, makes them safe, and this PR only changes when requests fail, not when memory is reclaimed. It must merge after #61667, and I'll rebase onto it then. Not a duplicate: the only open PRs referencing #63602 are #63628 (gap 4), #63664 (gap 5) and #63708 (gap 1). #61667 changes what happens to slots on timeout and close, but not whether the session survives a missed `AbortAck`. ## Test plan ``` venv/bin/pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/session/client.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/session/session.py tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_sessions.py ``` - New `TestClientFlows::test_load_abort_ack_timeout_disconnects_peer`: two loads in flight, and one misses its `AbortAck`. That load fails in the same poll. The session is dead with `death_reason == data_plane_fault == "abort ack timed out"`, a `DisconnectMsg` was sent, and `close()` fails the second load. - New `TestClientFlows::test_load_abort_ack_timeout_after_peer_disconnect_is_not_a_fault`: the peer's `DisconnectMsg` arrives in the same poll the `AbortAck` expires. The load fails, `death_reason == "peer disconnected"`, `data_plane_fault is None`, and no second `DisconnectMsg` is sent. - `test_load_abort_ack_clears_request` now also asserts that a received `AbortAck` leaves the session alive with no fault. ## Test results - `test_load_abort_ack_timeout_disconnects_peer` with the escalation call removed: fails (`assert not session.alive`). - `test_load_abort_ack_timeout_after_peer_disconnect_is_not_a_fault` without the liveness guard: fails (`AssertionError: assert 'abort ack timed out' is None`). - Full P2P suite (`tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p`): 327 passed, CPU-only. - pre-commit: passed (mypy skipped locally: the hook env runs Python 3.10). No model evaluation: this changes only failure handling toward a faulted peer, not outputs. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change. I reviewed every line and ran the tests above. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? @@ -855,6 +855,69 @@ def test_load_abort_ack_timeout_surfaces_failure(self):
         assert loads == [LoadResult(job_id=7, kv_request_id="req-7", success=False)]
         assert "req-7" not in session._client._requests
 
+    def test_load_abort_ack_timeout_disconnects_peer(self):
+        """A missed AbortAck faults the peer, so later fetches skip it.
+
+        The peer has stopped confirming that its WRITEs ended; keeping the
+        session would make every later load wait out both timeouts again.
+        Loads still in flight on the session fail through close().
+        """
+        session, conn, _ = _make_session()
+        _activate(session, conn)
+        session.request_blocks(
+            job_id=7, kv_request_id="req-7", keys=[OffloadKey(b"k")], block_ids=[0]
+        )
+        session.request_blocks(
+            job_id=8, kv_request_id="req-8", keys=[OffloadKey(b"j")], block_ids=[1]
+        )
+        _client_load(session, "req-7").submitted_at = (
+            time.monotonic() - _PD_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S - 1.0
+        )
+        session.poll()
+        assert session.alive
+
+        _client_load(session, "req-7").aborted_at = (
+            time.monotonic() - _ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S - 1.0
+        )
+        loads = session.poll().loads
+        assert loads == [LoadResult(job_id=7, kv_request_id="req-7", success=False)]
+        assert not session.alive
+        assert session.death_reason == "abort ack timed out"
+        assert session.data_plane_fault == "abort ack timed out"
+        assert conn._sent[-1][TYPE_KEY] == DisconnectMsg.TYPE
+
+        result = session.close()
+        assert result.failed_jobs == [8]
+        assert result.failed_req_ids == ["req-8"]
+
+    def test_load_abort_ack_timeout_after_peer_disconnect_is_not_a_fault(self):
+        """A session the peer already closed is not faulted by the ack timeout.
+
+        Faulting it would apply the data-plane reconnect backoff to a clean
+        disconnect.
+        """
+        session, conn, _ = _make_session()
+        _activate(session, conn)
+        session.request_blocks(
+            job_id=7, kv_request_id="req-7", keys=[OffloadKey(b"k")], block_ids=[0]
+        )
+        _client_load(session, "req-7").submitted_at = (
+            time.monotonic() - _PD_LOAD_TIMEOUT_S - 1.0
+        )
+        session.poll()
+
+        _client_load(session, "req-7").aborted_at = (
+            time.monotonic() - _ABORT_ACK_TIMEOUT_S - 1.0
+        )
+        conn.enqueue({TYPE_KEY: DisconnectMsg.TYPE})
+        sent_before = len(conn._sent)
+        loads = session.poll().loads
+        assert loads == [LoadResult(job_id=7, kv_request_id="req-7", success=False)]
+        assert not session.alive
+        assert session.death_reason == "peer disconnected"
+        assert session.data_plane_fault is None
+        assert len(conn._sent) == sent_before
+

             return
         self._disconnect(f"data plane: {fault}")
 
+    def _escalate_abort_ack_timeout(self) -> None:
+        """Fault the peer once one of its AbortAcks times out.
+
+        The timed-out load already failed in this poll's results. Without
+        this, the session stays up and every later fetch to the same stuck

+            return
+        req_id, round_seq = expired
+        self._abort_ack_fault = "abort ack timed out"
+        logger.warning(

+            "disconnecting peer session",
+            self.peer_id,
+            req_id,
+            round_seq,
+        )
+        self._disconnect(self._abort_ack_fault)
